description: The settings every repository shares. A version is proposed only once it has been public for two days, so that a release pulled or fixed in its first days never reaches a branch; seven days held back the releases of anything published more often than once a week. internalChecksFilter is already strict by default; it is stated so that the wait is read here as holding back the branch and the pull request themselves, not only a status check on them. platformAutomerge is off so that whatever a repository lets Renovate merge waits for the pull request's checks as Renovate sees them, without relying on the repository's auto-merge setting or branch protection

logLevelRemap.description: A repository that sets minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour to timestamp-optional for some dependencies has asked for them to go ahead without a release time, yet Renovate still warns each time it does so, and the warning lands among the Dependency Dashboard's repository problems. Reported as info, the expected behaviour no longer hides the real problems. Only these two messages are matched, so every other warning stays a warning
logLevelRemap.matchMessage: /^Some (release|upgrade)\(s\) did not have a releaseTimestamp, but as we're running with minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-optional, proceeding/

packageRules.description: The official ubuntu image is proposed without the two-day wait. Docker Hub gives a tag's last push as its release time, and the official ubuntu tags are pushed again every day or two, so a tag seldom looks two days old and an update would hardly ever be proposed. The rule is here for every repository, whether it uses the image today or not, so that a base changed to ubuntu later does not fall into the same trap. The name is matched as it is written, not as Docker Hub resolves it, so each way of writing the image is listed. The pull request's checks still have to pass

Workflows are already read by the github-actions manager. Grouping them keeps a handful of actions from arriving as a handful of pull requests, since they are updated together and reviewed the same way. Everything the manager reads is in the group, runners and the versions given to setup actions included. A repository that wants one of them on a branch of its own, such as a Node kept in step with its image, gives it another groupName in its own packageRules, which come after these
